manifest.title: Functional-KL Allocation at 75% and 50% Sparsity
manifest.description: A controlled re-validation of whether isolated-module causal KL can guide static per-projection Wanda budget allocation.

charts.title: 50% Stage-1 mean masked-token KL
charts.question: Does functional-KL allocation reduce held-out mean KL more than uniform and random allocation?
charts.rationale: A sorted bar comparison shows that the oracle is best on mean KL, but only narrowly ahead of the strongest random control.

blocks.body:
# Functional-KL Allocation at 75% and 50% Sparsity

Controlled oracle-allocation experiment and budget-relaxation re-validation

## Technical summary

At 50% sparsity, the functional-KL allocation improved mean KL, P90 KL, and NLL gap relative to uniform DLM-Wanda, but reduced top-1 agreement slightly. Against the strongest random seed, it won only mean KL and NLL gap among the four preregistered gate metrics; random remained better on P90 KL and top-1 agreement. The directional-validity gate therefore failed. This does not support the claim that the 75% result failed only because its budget was too tight.

## At 50%, the oracle helps versus uniform but is not uniquely better than random

The functional-KL variant has the lowest mean KL (0.143389) and NLL gap (0.101478). Random seed 20260907 has the best P90 KL (0.315628) and top-1 agreement (81.187%). The oracle's supplementary P95 KL is best (0.439291), but P95 was not part of the preregistered four-metric gate.

## Preregistered gate result

Relative to uniform, FunctionalKL-50-mild won 3/4 formal metrics: mean KL, P90 KL, and NLL gap. Relative to the best random result per metric, it won 2/4: mean KL and NLL gap. It lost P90 KL by 0.000359 and top-1 agreement by 0.156 percentage points to random seed 20260907. Consequently, medium/aggressive schedules were not tested and no 50% downstream evaluation was run.

## Exact budget and actuator size

Every 50% variant pruned exactly 3,489,660,928 of 6,979,321,856 prunable weights. Non-uniform schedules used 22 protected projections at requested sparsity 48%, middle projections at 50%, and 22 donors at an exact requested 55.459872%. Integer row-wise pruning produced an actual projection-deviation range of −2.001953 to +5.468750 percentage points. Random and oracle variants therefore used the same actuator magnitude and exact global budget.

## The 75% regime showed no functional-KL allocation advantage

At 75%, the selected random mild allocation beat the functional-KL mild allocation on mean KL, P90 KL, NLL gap, and top-1 agreement. Functional-KL mild was also worse than uniform on mean KL, NLL gap, and top-1 agreement, with only P90 KL improving.

## The 75% GSM8K mini screen was measurement-poor for ranking methods

Uniform, best random, and functional-KL each scored 0/100; reconstruction allocation scored 1/100. There were no invalid-answer cases. These near-floor counts do not support a functional-KL claim and full downstream evaluation was intentionally deferred.

## Controlled design

The model revision, DLM-matched Wanda calibration cache, unmodified local Wanda score, 224-module causal-KL ranking, 40 held-out DLM states, per-projection unstructured row-wise pruning, and evaluation implementation were reused. Only the global sparsity changed from 75% to 50%, and all 50% masks were regenerated. The exact 75% oracle groups were retained; three random allocations used fixed seeds and matched the oracle's projection-type and parameter-count composition.

## Limitations

This diagnoses a static allocation actuator, not the validity of causal module vulnerability itself. The causal map comes from isolated module perturbations, whereas a globally sparse model contains interactions among all 224 projections. The 50% differences are small and were not tested on GSM8K by design. P95 favors the oracle, but it was supplementary and cannot override the frozen four-metric gate.

## Interpretation

**Artifact-supported fact:** relaxing sparsity to 50% makes the oracle allocation modestly better than uniform on three fidelity metrics, while an equally sized random reallocation remains competitive.

**Statistical interpretation:** the causal-KL ordering does not deliver a robust, uniquely useful static projection-budget signal. The data reject a clean explanation in which 75% failed only because capacity was too constrained.

**Speculation:** joint-pruning interactions may break the transfer from isolated-module vulnerability to a static module budget, or the useful signal may need finer granularity than a single sparsity number per projection.

## Exactly one recommended next step

Stop the causal-KL-to-projection-allocation branch and run one preregistered **individual-weight criterion diagnostic** to test whether the established functional signal survives at the actual Wanda decision granularity before any new pruning method is implemented.

## Further question

Can a pre-pruning per-weight statistic distinguish the vulnerable weight choices inside a projection without relying on a projection-wide budget shift?
